name: Peugeot
overview: Historic French marque immortalized in Australian outback rallying and local CKD assembly of 403, 404, 504, and 505 models at Heidelberg and Clayton, Victoria.
australian_history: Peugeot's legendary Australian reputation was forged in 1953 when Ken Tubman and John Marshall won the grueling 6,500-mile Redex Round Australia Reliability Trial in an unpretentious Peugeot 203, astounding the nation. Demand surged, leading to local assembly at Martin & King (Clayton) and later Renault's Heidelberg plant in Melbourne. The 403, 404, 504, and 505 were all assembled locally with high Australian content. The 504 won Wheels Car of the Year in 1969 and became famous for absorbing horrific Australian corrugations thanks to its long-travel independent suspension. Local assembly concluded in 1986. Distribution transitioned through Ateco, Sime Darby, and Inchcape. Modern Peugeot excels with the 208, 308, 2008, 3008, and 5008 SUVs.

models.overview: The legendary French workhorses assembled in Melbourne for almost two decades. Revered across Australia for soaking up horrific outback corrugations with long-travel independent suspension, victorious in the 1970 Ampol Trial, and winning 1970 Wheels Car of the Year.

models.name: 205, 306, 208 & 308 GTi
models.overview: The aristocrats of French hot hatch engineering. For more than three decades in Australia, Peugeot's GTi lineage defined what a front-wheel drive performance car could achieve. From the featherweight, razor-sharp 205 GTi 1.9 that reset international benchmarks, through the passive rear-steering 306 GTi-6 with its class-first six-speed manual, to the Peugeot Sport-engineered 308 GTi 270 with Torsen LSD and massive Alcon brakes.

504-505.australian_market_notes: The 504 was assembled at Clayton and later Heidelberg alongside Renaults. Australian versions featured reinforced suspension towers, heavy-duty dust sealing, and local trim. The 505 followed in 1980, assembled in Heidelberg until local manufacturing ceased in 1986, continuing as an import until 1993.

205-308-gti.name: 205, 306, 208 & 308 GTi
205-308-gti.overview: The aristocrats of French hot hatch engineering. For more than three decades in Australia, Peugeot's GTi lineage defined what a front-wheel drive performance car could achieve. From the featherweight, razor-sharp 205 GTi 1.9 that reset international benchmarks, through the passive rear-steering 306 GTi-6 with its class-first six-speed manual, to the Peugeot Sport-engineered 308 GTi 270 with Torsen LSD and massive Alcon brakes.
205-308-gti.australian_market_notes: The 205 GTi arrived in Australia in October 1987. Despite strict Australian design rules mandating lower compression for unleaded fuel, its pure 880kg chassis, communicative unassisted steering, and adjustability on throttle lift-off won instant acclaim. The 306 GTi-6 followed in 1997, and the 208/308 GTi by Peugeot Sport concluded a golden era in 2020.

generations.summary: Universally heralded as one of the purest hot hatches ever created. Weighing just 880kg with all-independent trailing-arm rear suspension, 15-inch Speedline alloys, and an eager 1.9L all-alloy engine.
